key_insight: Finite-time Lagrangian transport structures in the mid-plane of a supersonic reacting shear layer organize scalar gradients and mixing, with attracting and repelling ridges occupying the same high-strain skeleton as geodesic LCS.
engineering_relevance: The findings help identify where mixing and reaction are most strongly controlled in compressible reacting flows, which is useful for designing and diagnosing propulsion and combustion systems.
method: Time-resolved forward/backward FTLE fields were computed from 3D DNS mid-plane data.
Operational FTLE-ridge skeletons were compared with Cauchy-Green-based hyperbolic geodesic LCS strainlines.
Transport skeletons were related to temperature, mixture fraction, and a reaction intermediate through scalar-conditioned statistics.
evidence_signal: The study uses time-resolved mid-plane data from a three-dimensional direct numerical simulation and evaluates ridge overlap, persistence, scalar-gradient enrichment, and lag relative to decorrelation and FTLE integration scales.
watch_item: Results are based on a constrained planar slice of a 3D flow, so inferred transport structures may miss out-of-plane effects and depend on finite-time window choices.
paper_title: Planar Lagrangian transport and scalar-gradient organization in a turbulent reacting shear layer
